source.title: Correcting Gradient-Based Circuit Localization via Interaction-Aware Backpropagation
source.authors: Joakim Edin; Casper L. Christensen; Róbert Csordás; T. Ruotsalo; Zheng-Xuan Wu; Maria Maistro; Jing Huang; Lars Maaløe

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates circuit-localization faithfulness on the IOI benchmark with GIM and compares circuit metrics, but does not reproduce the original head ablations or circuit analysis.
record.gate_note: The IOI results evaluate GIM-localized circuits, not the original 26-head circuit or its stated head roles. The paper also reports attention self-repair and feature-attribution results on other tasks; these do not test the IOI circuit versions. Table values for non-IOI tasks were not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study uses the MIB IOI task as a benchmark and reports only its own method's (GIM) circuit-localization scores against other methods. It never examines the original 26-head circuit, its head classes, backup heads, prompt variants, or whether methods recover the same circuit, so its results do not bear on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that GIM achieves state-of-the-art circuit localization on MIB and better gradient-based feature attribution. They also conclude that softmax-based attention self-repair makes standard attribution underestimate component importance.
record.recipe_differences: Uses GIM-modified Edge Attribution Patching and benchmark circuit metrics, rather than the original study's manual circuit analysis and head-level interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that CPR and CMD yield different comparative assessments: GIM outperforms other methods on most tasks by CPR, while it performs comparably to EAP-IG by CMD. IOI prompt distribution and ablation type are not varied.

fits_no_version.finding: Softmax redistribution produces attention self-repair. Ablating one of two high-weight positions with similar values barely changes output, while joint ablation does. The authors detected it 65–1200 times per input on feature-attribution tasks, not on IOI.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Attention self-repair through softmax redistribution within a head causes single-component attribution to underestimate importance.

fits_no_version.finding: On the MIB IOI task, GIM-modified EAP gives higher CPR than EAP, EAP-IG and other methods across GPT-2, Qwen-2.5, Gemma-2 and Llama-3.1. It is comparable to EAP-IG on CMD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Interaction-aware gradient attribution localizes more faithful IOI edge circuits than independent-perturbation methods.

record.problems: The IOI table results evaluate GIM-localized circuits rather than the original proposed circuit. No uncertainty is stated for the IOI CPR or CMD scores, and the study does not vary IOI prompt distributions or ablation types.
record.rows_left_out: Non-IOI feature-attribution, attention self-repair, and other task/model circuit-localization results were omitted because they do not test the named IOI circuit or IOI prompt variants.

untested.parts: No identification or test of the 26 heads, 7 classes, roles, or the faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria.
No name-mover ablation or backup-head analysis on IOI.
IOI is scored on Qwen, Gemma and Llama, but only as method CPR/CMD; there is no head-class or role comparison.
Methods are ranked by CPR/CMD, but circuit overlap or identity across methods is not compared.
The ablation type is fixed (counterfactual) and the prompt distribution is fixed (MIB public test). The metric difference concerns method ranking, not the IOI circuit's apparent faithfulness.
No name orders, templates or more-name prompts are tested.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's relation 'tests'/T2 and its V5 limits_scope label are not justified. The CPR vs CMD disagreement is about method rankings, and the authors attribute it to CMD's use of absolute values, which ignores the sign of attributions. The IOI results are benchmark scores for the authors' own method. The self-repair experiments use non-IOI datasets, so they do not test V2.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not identify or test the original 26 attention heads, seven classes, their stated roles, or the original circuit's faithfulness, completeness and minimality.
No ablation of the main name-mover heads or test of backup heads taking over their IOI role.
No test of whether the same IOI circuit is present across other models, sizes, checkpoints, or tasks.
Methods are compared on circuit-localization metrics, but the study does not test whether they recover essentially the same circuit, or compare the original circuit across ablation types.
The IOI circuit-localization results use counterfactual ablations and report CPR and CMD; the study does not vary IOI prompt distributions or ablation type.
No comparison of IOI name orders, templates, or prompts with more names.

rows.subject: GPT-2 120M
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated GIM-localized circuits with counterfactual ablations and integrated circuit performance ratio (CPR).
rows.measure: Integrated circuit performance ratio (CPR; higher is better)
rows.baseline: Faithfulness is defined relative to the empty circuit (all components ablated) and full network.
rows.note: This is the GIM IOI result. It evaluates a GIM-localized circuit, not the original 26-head circuit; the score alone does not establish the original circuit's properties.
rows.check: This is the study's own method compared with others (GIM CPR 2.24 on GPT-2 IOI, Table 1). It is a method-performance score for a GIM-localized edge circuit, not a measure of the IOI circuit's faithfulness, completeness or evaluation sensitivity. The value is read correctly (IOI GPT-2 column).

rows.subject: GPT-2 120M
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated GIM-localized circuits with counterfactual ablations and integrated circuit-model distance (CMD).
rows.measure: Integrated circuit-model distance (CMD; lower is better)
rows.baseline: Full faithfulness is the reference in the CMD definition; CMD of 0 is optimal.
rows.note: This is the GIM IOI result. The paper reports that GIM is comparable to EAP-IG on CMD overall, while it outperforms other methods on most tasks by CPR; the metrics have different objectives.
rows.check: This is the study's own method compared with others (GIM CMD 0.02 on GPT-2 IOI, Table 6). The CPR/CMD ranking difference concerns which localization method looks best, not how faithful the IOI circuit looks. It should not be linked to V5.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: IOI circuit localization evaluated with CPR and CMD
reader_labels.reason: The study evaluates the same GIM-localized circuits using distinct metrics and reports different comparative conclusions for CPR and CMD overall; r1 and r2 are the GPT-2 IOI metric results. It does not vary IOI prompts or ablation type.
